The big word and ring show the worst of memory, storage and flagged apps: green is fine, amber means watch, red means act. The ring in the launcher top bar shows the same colour.
How much RAM and storage is free. A bar turns amber, then red, as space runs low.
Apps from the Clean Your TV list that came back on, for example after an update. Open one and choose Disable, never Uninstall.
Could be stopped, and the journal
Apps that may slow the TV, each with its risk. The ones you stopped are listed with the date: open one to turn it back on.

Sends a small snapshot of the TV (memory, biggest processes, storage, which packages are on) to your AI through the PC, and shows the answer here. It needs the PC agent running and USB debugging on. If debugging is off, the add-on asks to turn it on first, and turns it off again once the answer is in.
If the AI proposes stopping apps, you choose Apply. A countdown starts: press All good to keep the change. If you do nothing, or the TV fails its check, everything is put back.
Every question and answer, newest first, kept on the TV. It opens without the PC.
All running processes with uptime, processor and memory. Android hides other apps from an add-on, so the PC reads the table and sends it here.
Opens the storage screen of the TV, where cached data can be cleared.
Asks first, then the PC restarts the TV.
Turns debugging on for 30 minutes, then off by itself. It needs a permission granted once from the PC: adb shell pm grant com.mauro.tv.monitor android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

1. On the PC, install Python 3 and the Android platform-tools (adb), and copy the add-on folder.
2. On the PC, run: python tv_ai_agent.py --setup, and fill in the page that opens.
3. On the PC, run: python tv_ai_agent.py TV-ADDRESS --apply --watch, and leave it open: without it the TV cannot reach the AI.
4. On the TV, choose Ask the assistant.

API address: where the request goes. Default https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages.
Model: which model answers. Default claude-sonnet-5-5.
API key: from your AI account. It is saved encrypted for your user on the PC and never sent to the TV. You can set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead; TV_AI_MODEL and TV_AI_URL also override the model and the address.
TV address: the IP address of the TV.
Seconds to confirm: time to press All good before a change is undone, from 20 to 600, default 60.
--apply: lets you apply what the AI proposes. Without it you only get a preview.
--auto: skips the question for low-risk changes; the countdown still runs.
--max: most packages disabled in one run, default 3.
--wait: seconds to wait for your answer to a proposal, default 300.
The AI can only choose three actions, and the code checks each one: disable a package from the suggested list, close a running app, or clear caches. System packages are never touched.
The request uses the Anthropic Messages format. Another AI works only through an address that accepts the same format and the same headers.

Marked with the small monitor: Ask the assistant, Details (and its refresh), Restart, and applying what the AI proposes (stopping an app, closing an app, clearing caches) with its undo. They need the PC on, the agent running (step 3) and USB debugging on while they work. No PC needed: status, memory and storage, flagged and suggested apps and the journal, History, this guide, Clear cache and the USB debugging button. The TV cannot reach the AI by itself: it has no internet access and never holds your key. If the agent window is closed, the TV says there was no answer after about 25 seconds.
= needs the PC on, with the agent running
A small monitor on a button or next to a title means it only works with the PC on and the agent running (step 3 of Connect your AI). Without a monitor, it works on the TV alone.
